summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified by direct execution. npm install clean (0 vulnerabilities, 2 packages). npm run build produces zero TypeScript errors. dist/ contains index.js + index.js.map. .gitignore correctly lists node_modules/, dist/, config.json. package.json bin declares { paralizer: dist/index.js }. tsconfig confirms ES2022 / Node16 / strict / sourceMap. comments.note: dist/index.js lacks the executable bit (-rw-r--r--). npm sets the bit during global install/link, so bin invocation works correctly. However, running dist/index.js directly without node will fail. Adding a postbuild script (chmod +x dist/index.js) would improve DX for local development.

summary: WP-001 code review PASS. All four files reviewed against maintainability, best practices, performance, and future-context dimensions. No blocking issues found. Implementation is minimal, correct, and well-structured for a foundation WP. One documentation-forward item raised regarding the Node16 module resolution requirement for .js import extensions.

comments.note: package.json has no 'main' field. This is acceptable for a pure CLI tool (invoked exclusively via bin), but if the tool is ever used as a library by another package it will fall back to Node's default resolution. No action needed now — worth revisiting if a programmatic API is added in a later phase.

QA flagged dist/index.js missing executable bit. Adding a postbuild script (chmod +x dist/index.js) would improve local DX, but chmod is Unix-only and would break Windows builds. Recommend documenting the workaround (npm link or node dist/index.js) rather than adding an OS-specific postbuild step.

[documentation-forward] tsconfig uses module: Node16 + moduleResolution: Node16, which enforces that all relative imports in TypeScript source files must include the .js file extension (e.g., import { foo } from './utils.js'). This is a project-wide convention that will catch contributors off-guard. Document this requirement in a CONTRIBUTING.md or in the project README under a 'Development Notes' section before the codebase grows.
